prompt:
ATTACHED IMAGES
2 images are attached to this request, in this order. They are referred to below by number.
Image 1 (Subject Image) is the main subject. Treat it as the exact source, not as inspiration. Use the real person or object from this photograph exactly as it appears. Keep the identity, face and facial structure, expression, hairstyle, body shape and proportions, pose, clothing, accessories and every distinguishing detail unchanged. You may cut it out from its original background, scale it evenly, and crop or position it as the layout requires. Do not distort, stretch, squash, warp, reshape, redraw, retouch, beautify, age or de-age it. Do not replace it with a similar-looking person or object, and do not add or remove details. Keep its original, natural colours, skin tones and lighting.

Image 2 (Background image) is the main subject. Treat it as the exact source, not as inspiration. Use the real person or object from this photograph exactly as it appears. Keep the identity, face and facial structure, expression, hairstyle, body shape and proportions, pose, clothing, accessories and every distinguishing detail unchanged. You may cut it out from its original background, scale it evenly, and crop or position it as the layout requires. Do not distort, stretch, squash, warp, reshape, redraw, retouch, beautify, age or de-age it. Do not replace it with a similar-looking person or object, and do not add or remove details. Keep its original, natural colours, skin tones and lighting.

OPENING INSTRUCTION

Use the attached subject image (image 1) as the only primary subject source and the attached background image (image 2) as the only secondary/background visual source.

Reconstruct the inputs into a fixed square 1:1 retro editorial collage inspired by late-20th-century newspaper graphics, photocopied magazine layouts, archival architectural illustration, rough cut-paper montage, and analog paste-up design.

The visual treatment, layout logic, magenta accent, monochrome printing, paper surface, halftone processing, and collage construction described below are fixed characteristics of the template. Do not derive a new layout or aesthetic from the input images.


INPUT REFERENCES

Primary content:
the attached subject image (image 1)

Secondary/background content:
the attached background image (image 2)

Use the subject image only for the main foreground subject.

Use the background image only for the environmental, architectural, structural, landscape, or contextual imagery behind the subject.

Do not introduce additional people, buildings, objects, photographs, illustrations, or scenery that are not reasonably derived from these two inputs.


SUBJECT / PRIMARY-CONTENT PRESERVATION

Preserve the recognizable identity and defining characteristics of the attached subject image (image 1).

For a person, preserve:
- facial structure
- expression
- hairstyle
- glasses or accessories
- clothing
- pose
- body proportions
- distinguishing features

For an object, product, sculpture, or other subject, preserve:
- silhouette
- proportions
- orientation
- major structural features
- surface characteristics
- distinctive recognizable details

Do not replace, redesign, beautify, caricature, or substantially alter the subject.

Convert the subject photograph into a bold high-contrast black-and-white printed cutout while retaining enough photographic information for immediate recognition.


COMPOSITION

Use a fixed square 1:1 composition.

Place the main subject large and visually dominant around the left-center of the frame.

The subject should occupy approximately 50–65% of the image height and should feel like a manually cut photographic piece pasted over the background.

Use a relatively close crop similar to an editorial portrait:
- head-and-shoulders or upper-body framing for a person
- an equivalently dominant crop for an object

Keep the subject slightly left of the exact center so that the right side remains available for the strongest background structure.

Create an irregular hot-magenta cut-paper shape immediately behind the subject's head and upper body.

The magenta shape should:
- extend slightly beyond the subject silhouette
- be clearly visible around the head, shoulders, or dominant contour
- have irregular angular hand-cut edges
- resemble colored paper physically pasted underneath the photograph
- remain a supporting graphic element rather than becoming a full background panel

Allow the subject to overlap the background imagery naturally.

Maintain visible negative space and avoid filling every part of the canvas.


BACKGROUND / SECONDARY-CONTENT TREATMENT

Use the attached background image (image 2) as the sole source for all contextual background imagery.

Preserve its most recognizable environmental or structural features, but reinterpret them into an archival printed illustration.

Transform the background image into a mixture of:
- fine black ink linework
- technical pen drawing
- architectural engraving
- newspaper illustration
- light photocopy degradation
- sparse halftone shading

The background must read primarily as illustrated or printed rather than as a clean full-color photograph.

Separate portions of the same the attached background image (image 2) across the composition when useful.

Place the strongest recognizable background structure mainly along the right third of the frame, extending vertically from the lower-right toward the upper-right.

A smaller secondary fragment from the same background may appear toward the upper-left behind the main subject, echoing the layered architectural montage visible in vintage editorial collage.

These fragments must still clearly originate from the same the attached background image (image 2); do not invent unrelated scenery.

Let sections of the background fade into the cream paper instead of enclosing the entire scene inside obvious rectangular photographic frames.


STYLE MATCHING

Create the appearance of a handmade editorial paste-up assembled from:
- photocopied portrait photography
- clipped newspaper images
- architectural pen drawings
- hand-cut colored paper
- aged publication stock
- imperfect analog printing

The subject should remain photographic.

The background should feel illustrated, engraved, sketched, or heavily print-translated.

The contrast between the photographic foreground subject and illustrated background is a defining characteristic and must remain visually obvious at a glance.

Use slightly imperfect alignment and physical layering so the collage feels assembled manually rather than generated as a seamless digital composite.

Include only a few restrained editorial marks:
- thin dashed curved trajectory lines
- tiny hand-drawn X marks
- extremely subtle clipped-paper fragments
- faint registration or printing imperfections

These marks are fixed supporting details and should never become infographic elements.


COLOUR TREATMENT

Use a highly restricted fixed palette:

1. Foreground subject:
   deep black, charcoal, faded black, warm paper-white

2. Background imagery:
   black, charcoal, faded grey-black, warm paper-white

3. Primary accent:
   vivid hot magenta / saturated editorial pink

4. Base surface:
   warm aged cream / pale ivory paper

The photographic subject must remain essentially monochrome.

The background must remain monochrome.

The hot-magenta paper shape should be the only strong saturated colour in the composition.

The colour separation between the black-and-white imagery, warm cream paper, and vivid magenta accent is mandatory and must be visually obvious at a glance.

Do not introduce additional accent colours.


LIGHTING AND TONAL TREATMENT

Retain the original lighting cues of the attached subject image (image 1) only where they help preserve facial or structural form.

Translate the subject into strong editorial black-and-white contrast:
- rich matte blacks
- slightly crushed dark shadows
- clear midtone separation
- pale printed highlights
- occasional blown or paper-white highlight areas

Do not create glossy cinematic lighting.

Do not add artificial rim lights, neon illumination, dramatic colored light, or modern studio effects.

The result should feel printed rather than digitally illuminated.

Keep the foreground subject sharper and heavier in contrast than the background.

The background should appear lighter, finer, and less visually dense so that it recedes behind the subject.


TEXTURE AND FINISHING

Apply authentic analog print texture throughout.

Foreground subject:
- medium-to-coarse halftone dots
- photocopy grain
- dry black ink texture
- slight tonal breakup
- faint newspaper screening
- occasional distressed edges

Background illustration:
- thin imperfect ink lines
- faded printed detail
- uneven line density
- subtle photocopy noise
- lightly broken ink

Magenta paper:
- matte printed-paper finish
- very subtle fiber texture
- slightly rough cut edges
- tiny analog imperfections

Base paper:
- warm pale cream
- fine paper fibers
- subtle speckling
- very mild age discoloration
- soft scanning noise

Keep the texture visible without making the image muddy.

The subject's important facial or structural details must remain readable beneath the print treatment.


STRICT REQUIREMENTS

- Output must always be square 1:1.
- Use only the attached subject image (image 1) for the foreground subject.
- Use only the attached background image (image 2) for the environmental/background imagery.
- Main subject must remain recognizable.
- Main subject must be a high-contrast black-and-white photographic cutout.
- Main subject must be positioned predominantly left-center.
- Background must be translated into monochrome archival ink / architectural-print styling.
- Strongest background structure should primarily occupy the right side.
- Include one irregular vivid hot-magenta paper shape directly behind the main subject.
- Preserve a warm aged cream paper base.
- Subject must visually sit in front of the magenta layer and background imagery.
- Maintain clear depth through physical-looking paper overlap.
- Keep the collage minimal and editorial rather than dense or decorative.
- Analog print imperfections must remain visible.
- Do not create a polished digital-vector appearance.


AVOID / NEGATIVE INSTRUCTIONS

Do not include:
- readable text
- headlines
- captions
- numbers
- letters
- typography
- logos
- signatures
- watermarks
- brand marks
- UI elements
- charts
- graphs
- infographic elements
- arrows
- labels
- excessive symbols
- multiple accent colours
- colorful background photography
- smooth digital gradients
- glossy 3D rendering
- modern vector illustration
- polished geometric UI graphics
- neon effects
- cinematic color grading
- excessive collage fragments
- decorative clutter
- unrelated objects
- additional people
- unrelated background imagery
- perfectly clean digital cutout edges

Do not allow the background to overpower the foreground subject.

Do not use the background image as another dominant photographic panel.

Do not recolor the subject magenta.

Do not replace the magenta paper accent with a glow, gradient, lighting effect, or transparent overlay.

The magenta area must visibly resemble a physical piece of colored paper beneath the subject.

ADDITIONAL ELEMENTS
Add the following to the composition. Keep the layout and hierarchy described above.
Apply a halftone texture pattern at Low intensity. Use a controlled grid of dots that converts tonal areas into halftone dot patterns while preserving the original shape, details, colors and information of the affected element.

Add scattered line cuts throughout the composition. Place some lines in front of the main subject and others across the background image, creating varied depth and visual interruption. Randomize the position, direction, length and spacing of the lines on every generation while keeping the composition balanced. Render every line cut in #E80909.

ADDITIONAL RULES
- {"condition":"always","instruction":"Scatter line cuts across both foreground and background areas."}
- {"condition":"always","instruction":"Randomize line placement, direction, length and spacing on every generation."}
- {"condition":"always","instruction":"Allow some lines to overlap the main subject while others remain behind it."}
- {"condition":"always","instruction":"Keep the lines visually distinct and avoid forming a regular grid or repetitive pattern."}
- {"condition":"always","instruction":"Use the selected color for all line cuts."}
- Use the subject from the attached image exactly as photographed. Do not distort, stretch, warp, redraw, retouch or replace it, and do not change its identity, features or proportions.
